demos_hosted.title: Eye Blink Detection
demos_hosted.subtitle: BlinkLinMulT
demos_hosted.content: Upload a video or use your webcam: the model scores eye closure per frame, per eye, and derives blink events from that signal. Runs the ONNX graph at 4.15 ms/frame.

demos_hosted.title: Personality Perception
demos_hosted.subtitle: PersonalityLinMulT
demos_hosted.content: Estimates perceived Big Five traits from speech. The demo exposes a live PyTorch-vs-ONNX backend switch, so you can compare the two runtimes on the same input.

demos_showcase.title: Annie
demos_showcase.subtitle: annie
demos_showcase.content: A local-first browser UI to explore, inspect, and validate a video annotation dataset side by side with its frame-wise labels. Runs entirely on your machine — no upload, no cloud.

demos_showcase.title: Personality Questionnaire
demos_showcase.subtitle: personality_questionnaire
demos_showcase.content: A localhost application to administer, score, and record validated personality and affect instruments (BFI-2, PANAS, VAS-F). Binds to 127.0.0.1 only — no data leaves the machine, by design.

practices.title: Model optimization
points: ONNX export gated on numerical parity: agreement to 4.8e-07 before a graph is allowed to ship.
4.9x faster inference, 20.19 to 4.15 ms/frame, measured rather than estimated.
A torch-free inference path saves 469 MB in deployment; a packaging test fails if that regresses.

practices.title: Deployment & containerization
points: Docker images serving the ONNX path, running identically on localhost and Google Cloud Run.
Cloud Run with true scale-to-zero, so an idle demo costs nothing.
FastAPI REST services and two public Gradio apps on Hugging Face Spaces.

practices.title: Experiment tracking & model lifecycle
points: MLflow tracking for every run, with the Model Registry as the promotion boundary.
Alias-based promotion (@champion, not deprecated stages), so a specific run becomes the deployable model through a deliberate, auditable step.
Optuna hyperparameter optimization and systematic feature-ablation matrices.

practices.title: Statistical rigor
points: "Model A scored higher" is not the same claim as "model A is better", so comparisons are tested, not tabulated.
Recording-clustered paired bootstrap resampling recordings rather than frames, with 95% confidence intervals.
Holm-corrected p-values across the whole family of pairwise comparisons.

practices.title: Reproducibility
points: Training reads a single HDF5 artifact, which is the reproducibility boundary.
That artifact embeds the builder config verbatim, the commit SHA, and the label hash, so a built file always traces back to what produced it.
Config-driven pipelines; licensed raw data is never redistributed, only derived features.

practices.title: Software quality & CI
points: 84-100% line coverage across the published packages, enforced in CI by Codecov, exercising every public entry point: the inference API, the ONNX and PyTorch runtimes, the CLI, and the packaging contract.

Tests are written against real use cases and reviewed by hand, not generated to inflate a number - a packaging test fails if the torch-free install regresses, and numerical-parity tests gate every ONNX export.
`make check` - ruff, ty, the full suite, and a docs build - is the same gate CI runs.
